description: We are a team of two passionate innovators who love technology, creativity, and solving real-world problems. We're excited to collaborate, learn, and build meaningful solutions at the NASA Space Apps Challenge!
summary:
Imagine being millions of miles from Earth. Your heart rate rises, your sleep has been poor, and you are feeling stressed. You notice something is different—but what does it mean when help from Earth cannot arrive immediately?

That question inspired **Orbit Vitals**.

Created by team FIIA, Orbit Vitals is an interactive web app designed to help astronauts better understand their health during long-duration space missions.

It brings six essential indicators—heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep, and emotional well-being—into one intuitive dashboard. Seven-day trends help users recognize changes, while clear explanations make complex health information easier to understand.

Our scenario simulator lets users explore how the dashboard responds to elevated heart rate, stress, and insufficient sleep. Sleep planning and an instant health overview make the experience more practical and accessible.

Inspired by NASA's research into human health in space, we believe astronauts deserve tools that make understanding their well-being simpler, especially when communication with Earth is delayed.

**Orbit Vitals is built on one simple idea: the farther we travel from Earth, the more important it becomes to understand ourselves.**
details:
ORBIT VITALS
Because every signal matters when Earth is far away.
THE CHALLENGE
What if the numbers are telling us something?
An astronaut wakes up after another night of poor sleep. Their heart rate is higher than usual. Stress is building. Individually, these changes might seem insignificant. But together, could they be telling a bigger story?
On Earth, asking for help can be as simple as making a phone call. During a mission far from Earth, communication delays can make that much harder.
And that made us wonder: what if astronauts could understand changes in their well-being more easily, without having to wait for someone else to interpret every number?
That question became Orbit Vitals.
FROM SCATTERED NUMBERS TO A CLEARER PICTURE
We are team FIIA, and we created Orbit Vitals, an interactive web application prototype that brings six aspects of astronaut health into one place: heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep, and emotional well-being.
But we didn’t want to build another screen filled with medical statistics.
We wanted to make those numbers meaningful.
Our dashboard lets users explore individual health indicators, follow changes over seven days, and read clear explanations of what different measurements may suggest.
Instead of treating each reading as an isolated number, Orbit Vitals helps users look at the bigger picture.
The interface also includes an at-a-glance health overview and sleep planning features, bringing useful information together without making the experience unnecessarily complicated.
EXPERIENCE IT FIRSTHAND
Don’t just read about it. Try it.
One of our favorite parts of Orbit Vitals is its interactive scenario simulator.
What happens when heart rate rises? What does the dashboard show when stress increases? How does insufficient sleep change the information presented to the user?
Rather than simply describing these situations, we wanted people to explore them.
The simulator demonstrates how Orbit Vitals responds to different health scenarios, allowing users to see how measurements, trends, and explanations work together.
We built the experience around simulated health data so that visitors can interact with the concept directly.
Our aim was simple: make the problem understandable, and make our proposed solution something you can actually experience.
WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE SCREEN
Space exploration is pushing humanity toward longer and more demanding missions. As astronauts travel farther from Earth, the ability to understand their own condition becomes increasingly important.
NASA’s research into human health during spaceflight helped inspire our approach.
We considered the challenges of delayed communication, changing physical and emotional well-being, and the importance of presenting information clearly when people may already be under pressure.
Our response was to focus on three things: clarity, awareness, and accessibility.
We are not trying to replace medical expertise. We are exploring how a better interface could help astronauts notice changes, understand patterns, and communicate their condition more effectively.
The distinctive part of Orbit Vitals is not a single measurement. It is the way different aspects of well-being are brought together into one understandable experience.
HOW WE TURNED OUR IDEA INTO REALITY
We developed Orbit Vitals as an interactive, browser-based prototype using Lovable to help build, refine, and publish the application efficiently.
Our team chose the problem, defined the project’s goals, selected the six indicators, shaped the user experience, and reviewed the features throughout development.
We also prepared an interactive six-slide presentation, using AI-assisted tools to support writing, visual development, and technical refinement while keeping the project’s direction and final decisions firmly in our hands.
We wanted to create more than a proposal on paper—we wanted a working demonstration of how our idea could look and feel.
LOOKING AHEAD
Where could Orbit Vitals go next?
Future development could explore connections with wearable health sensors, more detailed trend analysis, and research-based approaches to interpreting health information in isolated environments.
And although our inspiration comes from space, the problem is not limited to astronauts.
Researchers in remote stations, people working in isolated environments, and teams operating far from immediate medical support may face similar challenges in understanding and communicating health information.
That gives Orbit Vitals a purpose beyond a single mission.
We cannot eliminate the distance between astronauts and Earth. But we can explore ways to make the information they depend on easier to understand.
For team FIIA, that is what Orbit Vitals is about.
Not just collecting numbers.
Making sure those numbers tell a story worth paying attention to.
TOOLS & RESOURCES WE USED:
1. AI-Assisted Tools & Development Workflow
Lovable (https://orbit-vitality-watch.lovable.app/): Our main prototyping platform, used to develop the interactive dashboard with six navigation views, seven-day health trends, simulated lock-screen notifications, and color-coded alerts (green: nominal, yellow: caution, red: critical).
Google Gemini & Claude: Supported application architecture, code debugging, UI component refinement, and the creation of clear, low-cognitive-load health summaries for high-stress environments.
ChatGPT: Assisted with user stories, problem statements, project descriptions, and presentation development.
2. NASA Resources & Scientific Foundations
NASA Space Apps Challenge Theme & Guidelines: Guided our exploration of astronaut health, physiological adaptation to microgravity, communication delays, and autonomous decision-making during deep-space missions.
Aerospace & Space Medicine Monitoring Concepts: Informed our approach to cardiovascular monitoring, sleep quality, fatigue, and visual health alerts. These principles inspired the dashboard's trend tracking and color-coded warning system.
All AI-assisted work was reviewed by team FIIA, which remained responsible for the project's vision, development choices, and final decisions.
